title: Continuous integration test pipelines omit Go race detector, masking active data races in goroutine supervision
summary: Neither the CI test workflows (.github/workflows/ci.yml) nor Makefile test targets execute tests with the Go race detector (-race). A targeted probe with 'go test -race -short -timeout 30s ./pkg/bufferpool/... ./pkg/goroutinelabels/...' immediately fails with exit 1, exposing active data races in pkg/goroutinelabels.(*Pool).Stop() and Submit() across 6 test cases. Omitting -race from CI allows fundamental synchronization defects in core concurrency primitives to land undetected.
recommendation: Incorporate a dedicated -race matrix job in .github/workflows/ci.yml covering core concurrency and storage packages (pkg/goroutinelabels, pkg/concurrency, pkg/scheduler, pkg/storage), and resolve the channel send/close race in pkg/goroutinelabels/pool.go.
non_goals: Running the race detector on every single package in short developer smoke loops where build time overhead is prohibitive
Rewriting the entire goroutinelabels concurrency architecture

evidence.detail: CI unit-tests matrix runs go test -short -p 2 -timeout 8m without -race flag
Makefile test targets test-unit and test-unit-all omit -race flag
Targeted race probe fails with WARNING: DATA RACE in pkg/goroutinelabels.(*Pool).Stop at pool.go:235 and Submit at pool.go:183, failing 6 tests

citations.point: Testing Concurrency: Always test concurrent code with the race detector enabled (-race) in automated continuous integration.
Introducing the Go Race Detector: The race detector is an essential tool for finding synchronization bugs and race conditions in concurrent Go programs.

title: Ubiquitous hardcoded time.Sleep delays in asynchronous tests create severe CI flake risks
summary: Static analysis revealed 475 time.Sleep invocations across 216 test files, with 82 test files concurrently executing with t.Parallel(). Sleep durations range from 50ms up to 6 seconds (e.g. 6s in scenario_builder_id_stream_test.go:364, 4s and 2.5s in scheduler_test.go:443,583, and 3s in async_check_test.go:297). Under multi-job CI runner thread contention, arbitrary wall-clock sleeps routinely expire before background worker events complete, causing non-deterministic flakes and artificial CI test timeouts.
recommendation: Replace arbitrary time.Sleep calls with deterministic synchronization primitives, such as channels, sync.WaitGroup, or polling loops with short intervals bounded by explicit context timeouts (e.g. require.Eventually / assert.Eventually or waitForCondition).
non_goals: Removing intentional time-dilation tests that explicitly verify TTL expiration algorithms with mock clocks

evidence.detail: Test waits 6 seconds for watcher poll detection: time.Sleep(6 * time.Second)
Scheduler queue watch test sleeps 4000ms for retry backoff: time.Sleep(4000 * time.Millisecond)
Async check test sleeps 3 seconds waiting for retry completion: time.Sleep(3 * time.Second)
Census identified 475 time.Sleep calls across 216 test files, with 82 files combining t.Parallel() and time.Sleep

citations.point: Flaky Tests at Google and How We Mitigate Them: Sleep-based synchronization in tests is the leading cause of non-deterministic CI failures under resource contention.
Fast and deterministic feedback: Tests must synchronize on explicit state changes rather than real-world wall clock time.

title: Zero-assertion test stubs and unasserted accessor loops deployed to artificially satisfy TDD policies
summary: Repository-wide AST inspection identified 230 test functions with zero assertions (no assert.*, require.*, or t.Error/Fatal). Multiple test files explicitly contain comments confirming they were created solely to satisfy host TDD mandates without asserting behavior (e.g. cmd/zqk/mesh/mesh_test.go:6 '// Dummy test to satisfy TDD Mandate', pkg/swarm/executor_test.go:6 '// Simple test to satisfy TDD mandate', pkg/objects/field_keys_test.go:8 '// Stub test to satisfy TDD policy'). Additionally, over 160 extra_coverage_test.go files contain hundreds of unasserted _ = Accessor().Safe() calls (such as pkg/config/extra_coverage_test.go:11-123 running 110 unasserted property reads) purely to inflate line-coverage percentages.
recommendation: Implement a CI vet rule or linter (such as testifylint or a custom zqk-vet AST check) that rejects test functions with zero assertions. Refactor or delete empty TDD vanity stubs and replace vacuous _ = ... accessor sweeps with genuine property and default-value invariant assertions.
non_goals: Prohibiting lightweight sanity tests that verify non-panicking execution of complex initialization routines

evidence.detail: TestMesh is an empty function commented '// Dummy test to satisfy TDD Mandate'
TestExecutorInterface is an empty function commented '// Simple test to satisfy TDD mandate'
TestFieldKeysStub is an empty function commented '// Stub test to satisfy TDD policy'
TestExtraAccessorsAndLoaders executes 112 unasserted _ = ... accessor calls to inflate line coverage
230 test functions identified with zero assertions across repository; 160+ extra_coverage_test.go files

citations.point: Maintainability / Testability: Verification validity requires that test executions establish verifiable invariants rather than unasserted execution paths.
Test Coverage: Test coverage is a useful tool for finding untested code, but high coverage numbers achieved without meaningful assertions provide false confidence.

title: Storage delete audit logging bypassed in production and test suites via test-only environment backdoor
summary: Production code in pkg/storage/audit_events_ops.go explicitly checks zqkenv.SkipDeleteAudit().Get() == '1' to skip creating delete audit events. In pkg/storage/setup_test.go, the storage test suite unconditionally configures zqkenv.SkipDeleteAudit().Set('1') because delete audit events caused cascade delete tests to fail due to unresolved index visibility race conditions (documented as PRI-212). Consequently, the critical production delete audit path is never tested during cascade delete tests, and production deployments risk silent audit suppression if the variable is set.
recommendation: Remove the test-only zqkenv.SkipDeleteAudit environment check from production code in audit_events_ops.go. Fix the underlying index visibility race condition (PRI-212) in the storage engine so cascade delete tests execute with audit event creation enabled.
non_goals: Disallowing isolated test harnesses from disabling asynchronous sinks during unit benchmarks

evidence.detail: audit_events_ops.go checks test-only env var: if zqkenv.SkipDeleteAudit().Get() == '1' { return nil }
setup_test.go notes delete-audit Create path affects index visibility and unconditionally disables delete audit: zqkenv.SkipDeleteAudit().Set('1')

citations.point: Control 1.1: Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling - Security controls must fail closed and bypass mechanisms must not exist in production code.
Hermetic and Truthful Testing: Tests should run production code paths without test-specific production backdoors that hide concurrency bugs.

title: Adversarial concurrency and MCP stdio integration tests orphaned behind unexecuted build tags
summary: Integration tests tagged with //go:build integration (including pkg/storage/adversarial_concurrency_test.go, pkg/mcp/graph_integration_test.go, and pkg/mcp/mcp_server_stdio_integration_test.go) are orphaned and never executed. Neither .github/workflows/ci.yml nor Makefile targets pass -tags integration. The only target named test-integration in Makefile runs scripts/open-core/test-public-release-gates.sh, which merely checks release tarball packaging rather than executing Go integration tests. Consequently, adversarial multi-writer concurrency stress tests are never compiled or verified in CI.
recommendation: Add a dedicated integration-tests step or matrix job in .github/workflows/ci.yml and update Makefile test-integration to execute go test -tags integration ./pkg/... with adequate timeouts.
non_goals: Running long-running adversarial stress tests on every lightweight git pre-commit hook
Deprecating build tag isolation for heavyweight suites

evidence.detail: Adversarial concurrency stress test is gated behind //go:build integration
Makefile test-integration executes only test-public-release-gates.sh and omits go test -tags integration
CI workflow integration-tests job downloads binary and runs test-public-release-gates.sh without running Go integration test packages

citations.point: Maintainability / Testability: All operational tiers including integration tests must be integrated into continuous automated verification pipelines.
Continuous Integration Verification: Automated builds must execute integration suites continuously to prevent untested integration drift.

title: Complete absence of native Go fuzz testing across content-addressed storage, WAL, and parsers
summary: Across 7,547 Go files and 1.1M LOC spanning content-addressed storage (pkg/kernelcas), write-ahead logging (pkg/storage/wal), spec YAML deserializers, and MCP protocol parsers, there is not a single native Go fuzz test (func FuzzXxx(f *testing.F)). All parsing, hash integrity validation, frame decoding, and mutation pipelines rely exclusively on fixed unit test fixtures without randomized mutation-based robustness verification, leaving edge-case parser crashes and corruption handling untested.
recommendation: Introduce native Go fuzz tests (FuzzWALFrameDecode, FuzzKernelCASMutation, FuzzSpecYAMLParser, FuzzMCPToolCall) and integrate continuous fuzz testing into CI to identify malformed input vulnerabilities and edge-case corruption modes.
non_goals: Fuzzing external standard library or third-party dependency internals
Mandating 24-hour continuous fuzzing on local developer workstations

evidence.detail: Repository-wide AST scan across 2,912 test files returned exactly 0 fuzz tests matching func Fuzz
pkg/kernelcas/pipeline_test.go tests only fixed static strings without input mutation testing
pkg/storage/wal/object_wal_test.go tests deterministic write/read cycles without frame corruption fuzzing

citations.point: Practice PW.7.1: Perform dynamic vulnerability testing, including fuzz testing, on software components that handle untrusted inputs.
Go 1.18+ Fuzzing: Fuzzing is a type of automated testing which continuously manipulates inputs to a program to find bugs and edge-case panics.

title: Overwhelming reliance on non-specific error assertions permits spurious negative test passes
summary: Out of 14,731 error assertions in test files, over 14,200 (96.6%) use generic 'err != nil' or 'err == nil' checks, with only 154 errors.Is and 22 errors.As calls. In over 1,016 negative test cases asserting 'if err == nil { t.Fatal(...) }', tests succeed as long as any error is returned, without verifying sentinel error types, error codes, or failure reasons. Unrelated initialization, path, or permission failures cause negative tests to pass spuriously while masking underlying implementation bugs.
recommendation: Adopt specific error assertions using errors.Is, errors.As, or assert.ErrorIs / assert.ErrorContains across negative test cases, ensuring tests fail if an unexpected error occurs rather than the specific intended failure mode.
non_goals: Retroactively rewriting all positive err != nil happy path checks where any failure is fatal
Mandating sentinel errors for simple non-exported internal helper functions

evidence.detail: AST census: 14,233 generic err != nil checks and 1,016 err == nil checks vs only 154 errors.Is and 22 errors.As calls across tests
TestExtraCoverage_ObjectWALRegistry accepts any error without verifying error sentinel: if err == nil { t.Error(...) }

citations.point: Testing Errors: Tests that expect an error should check that the error is of the expected type or contains the expected message, not just that an error occurred.
Error Handling: Discriminate errors using errors.Is or type assertions to ensure proper failure handling and verifiable error contracts.

title: Asynchronous tests substitute test assertions with t.Log, masking queue and retry failures
summary: In asynchronous subsystem tests (e.g. cmd/zqk/system/async_check_test.go), verification logic after asynchronous operations does not fail the test upon observing invalid states. In TestAsyncValidation_RetryExhaustion and TestAsyncValidation_ProgressReporting, conditions where queueSize > 0 or !errorReceived.Load() are logged via t.Log and t.Logf rather than asserted with t.Error or t.Fatal. If retries stall or progress reporting fails completely, the test reports PASS, defeating the purpose of the test.
recommendation: Upgrade all speculative t.Log and t.Logf messages in test verification blocks to strict t.Errorf or t.Fatalf assertions, ensuring asynchronous invariants are strictly enforced.
non_goals: Prohibiting informative logging in tests when accompanied by strict assertions
Eliminating asynchronous validator queue test coverage

evidence.detail: Test logs message instead of failing when queue still has tasks: if queueSize > 0 { t.Logf(...) }
Test logs note instead of failing when error progress is not received or tasks remain in queue

citations.point: Testing on the Toilet: Assert What You Care About. Logging a failure without calling t.Error or t.Fatal turns a test into dead documentation that never catches regressions.
Automated Testing Invariants: Tests must produce binary pass/fail results based on invariant assertions.

title: Tests invoke unsynchronized os.Setenv without t.Setenv during parallel test execution
summary: While the vast majority of test packages have transitioned to t.Setenv (750 occurrences), 26 instances of unsynchronized os.Setenv remain in test files (e.g. pkg/testservices/services_extended_test.go:205, pkg/specialization/specialization_test.go:28, and pkg/zqkenv/env_alias_test.go:24). Unlike t.Setenv, os.Setenv directly mutates process-wide environment variables without Go test runner synchronization or automated cleanup, risking data races and test cross-talk when packages run concurrently.
recommendation: Replace all 26 instances of os.Setenv in *_test.go files with t.Setenv(key, val), ensuring automated test cleanup and panic prevention under parallel execution.
non_goals: Modifying TestMain functions where testing.T is unavailable and process-wide setup is deliberate

evidence.detail: Test sets ZQK_PROJECT_ROOT via os.Setenv without t.Setenv
Test sets environment variable via os.Setenv: _ = os.Setenv(envVar.Name(), tt.envVal)
Test mutates ZCOM_PROJECT_ROOT via os.Setenv without t.Setenv

citations.point: testing.T.Setenv: Uses Cleanup to restore the environment variable to its original value after the test. Panics if called in a parallel test to prevent data races.

title: Strong hermetic filesystem isolation via t.TempDir across 2,674 test fixtures
summary: The test codebase demonstrates exemplary filesystem hermeticity: 2,674 test functions strictly employ t.TempDir() and automated cleanup routines (t.Cleanup), ensuring that multi-agent storage workspaces, CAS caches, and WAL repositories execute in isolated transient directories without polluting the host environment, user directories, or developer working trees.
recommendation: Maintain strict enforcement of t.TempDir() across all newly added storage, daemon, and CLI test fixtures.
non_goals: Modifying existing hermetic test harness patterns

evidence.detail: Repository-wide census identified 2,674 calls to t.TempDir() across 689 tested packages
setupTestingFactoryCompleteTestEnvironment allocates fresh t.TempDir() and wires isolated test storage root

citations.point: Hermetic Tests: Tests must run in isolated environments without side-effects on shared filesystems or host machine state.
